title: Second Minimum Stack
description:
Design a stack `SecondMinStack` that supports standard stack operations plus retrieving both the smallest and the second smallest values currently in the stack in `O(1)` time.

Implement the `SecondMinStack` class:
- `SecondMinStack()` initializes an empty stack.
- `void push(int val)` pushes `val` onto the stack.
- `void pop()` removes the top element of the stack.
- `int top()` returns the top element of the stack.
- `int getMin()` returns the smallest value in the stack.
- `int getSecondMin()` returns the second smallest value in the stack (counting duplicates; e.g., for `[2, 5, 2]`, the sorted elements are `[2, 2, 5]`, so `getMin()` is `2` and `getSecondMin()` is `2`).
constraints: Methods pop, top, and getMin are called only when the stack has at least 1 element.
Method getSecondMin is called only when the stack has at least 2 elements.
At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made across all methods.
hints: Alongside each pushed value, store the running smallest (min1) and running second smallest (min2) at that stack depth.
When pushing val: if val < min1 then (newMin1, newMin2) = (val, min1); else if val < min2 then (min1, val); else keep (min1, min2).

examples.explanation: After pushing 5, 2, 8, sorted values are [2, 5, 8] -> min 2, secondMin 5; pushing 1 makes [1, 2, 5, 8] -> min 1, secondMin 2; popping 1 restores min 2, secondMin 5.
With duplicate minimums [3, 3, 7], both getMin and getSecondMin return 3.
Negative values and decreasing pushes update min1 and min2 in O(1) per operation.
